messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure game.
- Update its story to follow the boy who opens a forest door, is transported to another world, learns of a prophecy, and must collect five keys from five nations to return home.

## Requirements
- User requested a playable game for phones/tablets, then specified the story premise and key-collection goal.
- Do not copy Swordigo’s characters or assets; the existing game uses original branding and artwork.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Expressed the new story through the opening text and the ending reached at the current level’s gate; five nations/keys are described as the larger quest.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a side-scrolling game with movement, jumping, sword combat, enemies, coins, checkpoints, health, pause/restart, and mobile touch controls.
- Updated the opening story and gate ending to mention the other world, the girl, the king, the prophecy, five nations, bosses, and five keys.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully; browser loaded the page without console errors.

### Active
- The requested full five-nation/five-key adventure is not implemented as gameplay; only the story setup and ending narration describe it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If continuing the feature, implement playable progression through five nations, boss encounters, key collection, and a portal-home conclusion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation and updated story text.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-story.jpg`.

## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure game.
- Tell the story of a boy transported from a forest into another world, where he must collect five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- The game is implemented as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions are named Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression with guardians, key collection, gates, region-specific palettes, and a portal-home ending.
- Added the prophecy and origin story to the opening text and a five-key HUD and region quest text.
- JavaScript syntax checked; page reloaded and started in the browser with no console errors.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression, including guardian fights, gates, checkpoints, and the final ending; only initial browser play was tested.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test the five-region gameplay loop and fix any progression or combat issues found.
2. Check mobile/tablet layout and controls after the HUD additions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game, story, rendering, controls, and progression implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Latest change standardizes each region’s second checkpoint y-coordinate to `430`.
- Browser screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-five-nations.png`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure about a boy transported from a forest into another world, collecting five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- Implement the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions: Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, prophecy/origin story, HUD, quest text, and portal-home ending.
- Added death recovery at the last checkpoint and barriers at locked nation gates.
- Made sword attack repeat while held, so players can land successive hits without tapping for every strike.
- Adjusted the mobile HUD at widths up to 540px: status panel sits below the brand and quest text below both.
- JavaScript syntax checked; Playwright confirmed the initial mobile layout has no brand/status overlap and that movement collects coins.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression and fix any combat, movement, checkpoint, or gate issues found.
- Verify that death recovery and checkpoint placement work as intended.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Investigate remaining combat/progression issues: recent simulated play did not defeat Mossfang, and the player repeatedly reached the death screen.
2. Re-test boss fights, gate transitions, checkpoint recovery, ending, and mobile controls after fixing gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source, story, rendering, controls, HUD, and progression.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `index.html` and other untracked project files.
- `hurt(true)` now respawns at the platform floor matching the checkpoint’s x-coordinate rather than always using the world ground.
- At 390×844, `.brand` occupies y=12–43, `.status` y=52–96, and `.quest` y=104–143.
- Simulated gameplay collected three coins without losing health but did not advance to the guardian; a separate movement-plus-attack simulation ended at “Not the end.”

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure about a boy transported from a forest into another world, collecting five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- Implement the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions: Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, story, HUD, quest text, and portal-home ending.
- Added death recovery at the last checkpoint and barriers at locked nation gates.
- Made sword attacks repeat while held.
- Adjusted the mobile HUD layout for narrow screens.
- Identified gaps between platforms that caused falls; extended a platform across one gap and increased starting health from 3 to 5.
- Reduced common enemies to one hit and broadened their attack proximity.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully after changes.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression; guardian combat has not yet been demonstrated to work, and recent simulations lost health before reaching Mossfang.
- Continue tuning combat reach and damage feedback, then verify all region gates, checkpoints, death recovery, ending, and mobile controls.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix the guardian hit detection and attack timing; the latest change increased the sword animation’s progress denominator from `.24` to `.36`, but gameplay remains unverified.
2. Remove temporary `window.__debug` instrumentation from `index.html` when testing is complete.
3. Re-test long-form progression and mobile HUD/controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source, story, rendering, controls, HUD, and progression.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously listed as untracked.
- Playwright simulations showed the player can reach later sections but still loses health and has not reached or defeated the first guardian.
- `basePlatforms` now extends the platform at `x:790` from width `360` to `620`; player starts with 5 HP; common enemies have 1 HP and a wider hit radius.
- Temporary `window.__debug` exposes player, boss, coin, and screen state for browser tests.

## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired adventure in `index.html`, then change its gameplay to a true isometric angle.

## Requirements
- Playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.
- The player chose true isometric gameplay: move in four directions across angled ground, adapting platforms, enemies, and camera.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained HTML canvas game.
- The story spans five regions, each with a guardian and key; collecting all five opens the portal home.
- Replace vertical platforming with true isometric movement, rather than only tilting the visuals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, story, HUD, checkpoints, death recovery, and portal-home ending.
- Improved sword combat timing and damage feedback; browser simulation confirmed all five guardians can be defeated and the ending reached.
- Added jump buffering/coyote-time logic, increased player health, and tuned common enemy health and reach.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully.

### Active
- Convert the existing 2D platform game into true isometric gameplay and update mobile controls accordingly.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Refactor movement and world coordinates from horizontal platforming to four-direction isometric movement.
2. Adapt terrain, collision, enemies, guardians, gates, camera, rendering, and controls for the isometric world.
3. Re-test full progression, ending, and mobile/tablet playability.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source and the primary file to update.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously untracked.
- `index.html` still contains the original platformer, including temporary `window.__debug` instrumentation that should be removed after testing.
- Current touch controls are left/right, attack, and jump; keyboard controls are left/right, jump, and attack.

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

## Objective
- Transform the existing Swordigo-style game from 2D into a genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG.
- First provide a technical assessment and implementation plan; make no changes until the user approves.

## Requirements
- Inspect the existing project before changing anything.
- Address its language/framework, rendering engine, 3D capabilities, models/animation/shadows/collision, mobile controls, eight-direction movement, and safest upgrade or migration strategy.
- Do not modify or delete files before approval.

## Decisions
- No migration or implementation approach has been approved yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected project files and `index.html`; no files were changed during the latest request.
- Identified the current game as a single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript game using Canvas 2D and custom game logic, not Phaser, Three.js, Babylon.js, or another 3D engine.
- Identified mobile controls as HTML buttons wired through Pointer Events, with four discrete directions and an attack button.
- Found four-direction input normalized diagonally in the update loop, so it already supports eight directional movement directions at a basic level, but uses digital rather than analog input.

### Active
- Provide the requested clear technical assessment and staged implementation plan, including a safe migration strategy that preserves existing working features.

### Blocked
- Implementation is pending the user’s approval.

## Next Move
1. Explain that Canvas 2D can simulate an isometric look but does not provide genuine 3D rendering or built-in 3D character rigs, skeletal animation, 3D shadows, or 3D collision.
2. Recommend a migration path—likely Three.js for a browser-based project—with an orthographic camera, 3D scene/assets, animation and collision systems, and retained HTML HUD/mobile controls.
3. Propose staged implementation that keeps the current game as a working baseline and ports gameplay systems incrementally; make no file changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire current game implementation, including Canvas 2D rendering, gameplay, UI, and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project description; identifies the project as created with OMGithub.

## Important Context
- The project contains no package manifest or installed game-framework setup; the game is presently self-contained in `index.html`.
- Current touch movement is a four-button directional pad, not a joystick; attack is a separate touch button.
- Current movement combines two digital axes and normalizes their vector, allowing cardinal and diagonal movement.

content.text:
## Technical assessment

1. **Language and framework:** The game is written in HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. It is currently a self-contained browser game rather than a project built around a game framework.

2. **Rendering engine:** It uses **HTML Canvas 2D** and custom game logic. There is no current use of Phaser, Three.js, Babylon.js, or another 3D engine.

3. **Genuine 3D and an isometric camera:** Canvas 2D can draw an isometric-looking scene, but it does not provide a genuine 3D scene or camera. A 3D engine such as **Three.js** can render actual 3D geometry with an orthographic camera positioned at an isometric angle.

4. **Models, animation, shadows, and collision:** These are all feasible after adding a 3D engine. Three.js can load 3D character and environment assets, including skeletal animations in formats such as glTF/GLB. Shadows and 3D collision are also possible, but they require implementation and performance tuning; they are not features the current Canvas renderer provides. A physics library such as Rapier could handle collision and movement, or a smaller custom system could suit a simpler game.

5. **Current mobile controls:** The game uses HTML buttons and Pointer Events for directional movement and attacking. It has a four-button directional pad, not an analog joystick.

6. **Eight-direction movement:** The existing movement combines horizontal and vertical input and normalizes diagonal movement. That already allows movement in eight directions, but it is **digital**—players press combinations of discrete buttons rather than steering smoothly. For analog movement, replace or supplement the directional pad with a touch joystick that tracks pointer position and applies a dead zone and normalized input. In the 3D version, movement should also be mapped consistently to the camera’s ground plane.

## Recommended migration plan

The safest path is to preserve the existing game as a working reference and introduce Three.js incrementally, rather than trying to convert the Canvas renderer in place all at once:

1. **Preserve a runnable baseline.** Keep the current game intact while establishing a separate 3D entry point or branch of the implementation. Avoid removing current controls, UI, or gameplay until their replacements work.
2. **Set up the 3D foundation.** Add a Three.js scene, renderer, isometric orthographic camera, resize handling, and a simple test environment. Confirm this runs in the project’s existing deployment setup before committing to a larger build-system change.
3. **Port gameplay in stages.** Bring over movement and camera follow first, then collision and level geometry, combat and enemies, and finally progression and other game systems. Keep the existing HTML HUD and touch controls where practical.
4. **Add assets and animation.** Integrate 3D character and environment models, then connect animation states to gameplay actions. Add lighting and shadows with mobile performance in mind.
5. **Verify and retire deliberately.** Test desktop and mobile controls, movement in all directions, collisions, and performance. Keep the 2D version available until the 3D game reaches feature parity or you explicitly decide to replace it.

**Bottom line:** The current game does not provide genuine 3D itself, but the browser project can be upgraded to do so. Three.js is a practical fit for a browser-based 3D game with an orthographic isometric view. The existing controls and gameplay can be retained as a baseline while the 3D version is built and validated.

No files have been modified or deleted.

- Use Three.js for genuine 3D rendering.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Integrate Three.js as an ES module with an import map to `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.

- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attack input, and input release handling in `game.js`.

### Active
- Validate runtime behavior, gameplay, camera framing, collisions, and mobile performance.
- Fix any issues discovered during browser testing.

### Blocked
- Browser/runtime validation has not yet been performed.

## Next Move
1. Run the game through the project’s available browser workflow and check console/runtime errors.
2. Test desktop keyboard gameplay and mobile joystick plus attack, including pointer cancellation and simultaneous touches.
3. Verify camera framing, movement, collisions, combat, and performance; fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation and gameplay/input logic.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The previous Canvas 2D game was replaced at the entry point; its original snapshot remains in `index.html.backup`.
- `game.js` imports `three` through the import map added to `index.html`; serving the page over HTTP is needed for module loading.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for genuine 3D rendering.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Integrate Three.js as an ES module with an import map to `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html.backup` as a snapshot of the original game.
- Added a Three.js implementation in `game.js` with scene, camera, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, and UI integration.
- Updated `index.html` to load `game.js` as a module and provide a mobile joystick and attack control.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attack input, and input release handling.
- Served and opened the game in Playwright at `http://localhost:3002`; title screen and gameplay rendered, and starting the game worked.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser reported zero console errors.

### Active
- Validate runtime behavior, gameplay, camera framing, collisions, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- Browser emitted WebGL performance/feedback-loop warnings during screenshot capture; their impact and whether they indicate an issue remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect gameplay and title screenshots; verify the scene framing and rendering.
2. Test desktop keyboard gameplay, collisions, combat, and camera follow.
3. Test mobile joystick and attack, including pointer cancellation and simultaneous touches.
4. Investigate the WebGL warnings and address any functional or performance problems.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation and gameplay/input logic.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The previous Canvas 2D game was replaced at the entry point; its original snapshot remains in `index.html.backup`.
- Playwright showed WebGL2; no console errors were reported, but screenshot capture produced five WebGL warnings.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for genuine 3D rendering, loaded as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` to load the module and provide mobile joystick and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attack input, and input release handling.

4. Investigate whether the WebGL warnings persist outside screenshot capture.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation and gameplay/input logic.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

- The previous Canvas 2D game was replaced at the entry point; its original snapshot remains in `index.html.backup`.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attacks, and input release handling.
- Adjusted portrait mobile camera framing to use a 16-unit view height in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed gameplay starts, desktop movement input leaves the game running with full health, and Escape pause/resume works.
- Confirmed mobile controls fit within the 390×844 viewport.
- Clean reload and start produced no console warnings; no JavaScript errors observed.
- Captured screenshots including `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-mobile-input-test.png`.

### Active
- Validate actual joystick and attack pointer interactions, combat, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Assess the occasional WebGL warning during pointer/drag testing.

### Blocked
- Browser drag testing does not establish reliable real multitouch/joystick behavior; touch interaction and simultaneous movement/attack remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Test joystick movement, pointer cancellation/release, and simultaneous joystick-plus-attack input with appropriate touch events or a real mobile device.
2. Verify combat hits, obstacle collision, and camera follow in gameplay.
3. Investigate whether `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` recurs during ordinary play; it appeared once during mobile drag testing but not on clean reload/start.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, and portrait camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Desktop keyboard checks used synthetic browser `KeyboardEvent`s; mobile drag testing reset the joystick afterward but did not prove movement or multitouch behavior.
- Earlier screenshot captures showed `GPU stall due to ReadPixels` and `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop`; recent clean reload/start had no warnings, while one drag test reproduced the blit warning.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attacks, and input release handling.
- Adjusted portrait mobile camera framing to use a 16-unit view height in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed gameplay starts, Escape pause/resume works, and mobile controls fit within the 390×844 viewport.
- CDP touch tests confirmed joystick movement, simultaneous joystick-plus-attack input, separate joystick release while attack remains pressed, and final input release/reset.
- Clean reload/start and later touch checks produced no JavaScript errors or console warnings.
- Captured mobile input screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-mobile-input-test.png`.

### Active
- Validate combat hits and solid-obstacle collision in gameplay.
- Inspect camera-follow screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/camera-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/camera-after.png`.
- Determine whether the intermittent WebGL blit feedback-loop warning recurs during ordinary play.

### Blocked
- No real Android device test has been performed; browser touch emulation confirms simultaneous controls but not device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the camera screenshots and verify the camera follows the player during movement.
2. Run focused gameplay checks for enemy/boss hits and obstacle collision; previous attack attempts did not produce conclusive results.
3. Continue observing WebGL output for `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.`
4. Test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, and camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Desktop keyboard checks used synthetic browser keyboard events.
- CDP touch emulation verified joystick travel (knob transform `matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 32, 0)`) and simultaneous attack; controls reset on release.
- The WebGL warning recurred in earlier touch-event testing but did not appear during the most recent touch check.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, and mobile control fit via browser testing.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks produced no JavaScript errors or console warnings in recent runs.

### Active
- Validate combat hits and solid-obstacle collision in gameplay; prior attack tests were inconclusive.
- Inspect camera-follow screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/camera-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/camera-after.png`.
- Check whether the intermittent WebGL blit feedback-loop warning recurs during ordinary play.

### Blocked
- No real Android device test has been performed; browser touch emulation confirms simultaneous controls but not device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Inspect camera screenshots and verify the camera follows the player during movement.
2. Run focused gameplay checks for enemy/boss hits and obstacle collision.
3. Observe WebGL output for `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.`
4. Test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, and camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Desktop keyboard checks used synthetic browser keyboard events.
- CDP touch emulation verified joystick travel, simultaneous attack, independent input release, and control reset.
- Recent diagonal movement-and-attack testing did not conclusively demonstrate combat hits.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.
- Let an active attack hit nearby enemies without requiring the enemy to remain in front of the hero; approach and enemy movement can otherwise make hits miss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented the Three.js game, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, and joystick/attack input handling.
- Fixed combat hit registration by removing redundant directional checks from the enemy and boss attack triggers; controlled testing confirmed enemy health decreased and an enemy was defeated.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest combat edits.

### Active
- Verify solid-obstacle collision and camera follow in gameplay.
- Check whether the WebGL feedback-loop warning recurs during ordinary play.
- Remove temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics from `game.js`.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser touch emulation does not confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Remove `window.__debugGame` from `game.js`.
2. Run controlled gameplay checks for obstacle collision and camera follow; inspect the saved screenshots if useful.
3. Recheck for the WebGL feedback-loop warning and run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
4. Test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, camera follow; includes temporary diagnostics.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/follow-before.png`: Gameplay screenshot before movement.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.
- Improve the hero’s procedural animation quality, including locomotion, turning, foot placement, and jump phases, without replacing the existing character.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mobile performance in mind.
- Animations should smoothly blend based on movement speed; idle, walking, and running should look natural, and the character should face movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases; retain the existing character.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Use procedural animation because the current character has no skeletal rig.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining attack controls.
- Let active attacks hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, joystick/attack input handling, and combat hit registration.
- Verified obstacle collision and camera follow; controlled combat test verified enemy HP reduction and defeat.
- Removed temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics.
- Began procedural animation upgrade in `game.js`: introduced torso/head/arm/leg pivots, foot meshes, movement/jump state fields, eased turning target, and an `animateHero()` animation routine for blended gait, idle breathing, arm/leg swing, attacks, and jump/landing poses.

### Active
- Finish and integrate the animation update: call `animateHero()` from the game loop, implement or connect jump phase/state transitions, and verify model transforms and attack compatibility.
- Validate the new animation behavior in a browser and run syntax/diff checks.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser touch emulation cannot confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `game.js` edits, integrate `animateHero()` into `update()`, and ensure jump phases can be entered and completed.
2. Run `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser checks for idle, movement transitions, rotation, attacks, and jumping.
3. If possible, test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, controls, collision, camera follow, and in-progress procedural animation changes.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in Git.
- The latest animation edits have not yet been validated; `animateHero()` was added but is not yet called from the game loop.
- Jump animation state fields and pose handling exist, but no jump input/state transition was added, and the mobile jump control is currently hidden.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural animation, including locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump phases.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mobile performance in mind.
- Blend animations smoothly by movement speed; idle, walking, and running should look natural, and the character should face movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases; retain the existing character.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Use procedural animation because the current character has no skeletal rig.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining attack controls.
- Let active attacks hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.
- Add a mobile jump button alongside keyboard Space jump.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, joystick/attack handling, combat hit registration, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Controlled combat test verified enemy HP reduction and defeat.
- Removed temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics.
- Restructured the existing hero model with torso, head, arm, and leg pivots; added feet and procedural idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses.
- Connected `animateHero()` to gameplay updates and added keyboard-Space and mobile-button jump input with takeoff, airborne, and landing transitions.
- Enabled the mobile jump button in `index.html` and updated the controls hint to mention Space for jump.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Headless Chromium loaded the page and produced a 390×844 mobile screenshot; no clear game runtime exception was observed.

### Active
- Validate animation transforms and attack compatibility in a browser, including jump phases and simultaneous joystick/attack/jump input.
- Inspect the mobile screenshot/control layout and resolve any pose or gameplay conflicts.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run interactive browser checks for idle, movement transitions, rotation, attacks, and takeoff/airborne/landing.
2. Check simultaneous mobile joystick, attack, and jump input; adjust layout or animation if needed.
3. Test on a real Android device if available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, hero procedural animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in Git.
- Jump is mapped to keyboard Space and a mobile button; mobile controls now include joystick, attack, and jump.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural animation, including locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump phases.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mobile performance in mind.
- Blend animations smoothly by movement speed; idle, walking, and running should look natural, and the character should face movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases; retain the existing character.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Use procedural animation because the current character has no skeletal rig.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining attack controls.
- Allow active attacks to hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.
- Add a mobile jump button alongside keyboard Space jump.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, joystick/attack handling, combat hit registration, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Restructured the existing hero model with torso, head, arm, and leg pivots; added feet and procedural idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses.
- Connected `animateHero()` to gameplay updates and added keyboard-Space and mobile-button jump input with takeoff, airborne, and landing transitions.
- Enabled the mobile jump button in `index.html` and updated the controls hint to mention Space for jump.
- Interactive Chromium checks confirmed movement animation, turning, jump takeoff/airborne/landing, jump-and-attack compatibility, and simultaneous joystick/attack/jump input; no JavaScript exceptions observed.
- Removed the forward-facing attack restriction so nearby targets can be struck.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Remove the temporary `window.__testGame` diagnostic hook added to `game.js` for browser animation checks.
- Review final changes and verify syntax/diff cleanliness after removing the hook.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Remove `window.__testGame` from `game.js`.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; review `git status`.
3. Test on a real Android device if available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, hero procedural animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in Git.
- Jump is mapped to keyboard Space and a mobile button; mobile controls include joystick, attack, and jump.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.
